title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: the continuous batcher scheduler occasionally allowed long-lived queues from high-throughput customers to monopolize GPU cycles, causing starvation for low-throughput interactive requests and sporadic timeout spikes. This PR tunes the scheduler to improve fairness across routes/customers, adds explicit starvation prevention, and introduces adaptive timeouts that reduce wasteful requeues while preserving latency SLOs. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce multi-tenant queue prioritization: requests are tagged with a tenant priority score derived from route SLA and recent observed latency; scheduler uses a weighted fair-queueing approximation to pick batches. 2) Starvation prevention token bucket: each queue gets a starvation-credit counter that forces selection if a queue has been deferred beyond a hard threshold. 3) Adaptive per-batch timeout: timeout is dynamically adjusted based on observed kernel startup variance and recent batching delays to minimize premature cancellations. 4) Metrics and tracing: add per-queue wait_time, starvation_count, selection_score, and timeout_adjustment tags to facilitate debugging and SLO analysis. 5) Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for priority scoring and starvation logic, integration canary harness updates and perf microbenchmarks showing improvements. Design notes: - The weighted fair-queueing is an approximation (cheap computation) to avoid adding significant CPU overhead per scheduling decision. - Starvation threshold is configurable per deployment and tuned via the new runtime config: continuous_batcher.starvation_threshold_ms (default 1200ms). - Adaptive timeout uses an EWMA of kernel start latency (window=2000 samples) and clamps adjustments to +/-25% of base_timeout to avoid oscillation. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag (continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2). Start with internal Dedicated clusters, run perf-canary for 24h, then enable in hosted with canary traffic 1%. Revert plan: feature-flag off and config rollback. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless flag enabled. Checklist: - [x] Design review complete (ENG-9123) - [x] Performance benchmarks attached - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Metrics & dashboard changes documented - [x] Configurable via runtime flags - [x] Canary rollout plan included

release_notes: Improve continuous batcher scheduler fairness and prevent queue starvation; introduce adaptive timeouts to reduce spurious requeues. Configurable via continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 and continuous_batcher.starvation_threshold_ms. Backwards compatible and disabled by default.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 in a canary subset first. Monitor metrics: continuous_batcher.queue_wait_ms, continuous_batcher.starvation_count, continuous_batcher.selection_score and p99 request latency. If EWMA oscillation detected, reduce EWMA alpha or increase clamp window. Default starvation_threshold_ms=1200ms.
notes: This PR is part of a larger effort to stabilize continuous batching under mixed workloads. Follow-up work: UI for runtime config (ENG-9254), long-tail per-tenant autoscaling (PERF-4678).
